items.title: The role of circadian clock dysfunction in Alzheimer disease pathogenesis
items.author: Erik S. Musiek
items.content: Disruption of daily rhythms and circadian function has been linked to Alzheimer disease (AD). Sharma and Musiek explore this relationship, outlining the evidence for altered circadian clock function in AD and AD models and discussing the mechanisms through which circadian changes may contribute to disease pathogenesis.

items.title: Priming future aggression via vicarious experience
items.author: Jake Rogers
items.content: A common inhibitory plasticity mechanism in mice observing or directly engaged in aggression shapes shared behavioural responses in subsequent bidirectional aggressive interactions.

items.title: Making memories generalizable
items.author: Jake Rogers
items.content: Circuit level mechanisms are revealed in mouse hippocampus that support the use of orthogonal dimensions in the population activity geometry for representations to discriminate and generalize between related spatial task contexts.

items.title: The what, how and where of statistical learning: a neurocognitive synthesis
items.author: Michael T. Ullman
items.content: The capacity to learn regularities in the environment, known as statistical learning, underpins many cognitive abilities. Focusing on three well-established sequential statistical learning tasks, in this Review, Conway et al. consider how statistical learning may be most usefully defined and review the evidence for the involvement of specific learning processes and neural circuits.

items.title: Rewiring cancer: peripheral nerves control tumours
items.author: Paola D. Vermeer
items.content: Neural regulation of cancer is increasingly recognized as a fundamental component of cancer biology, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this Review, Vermeer and colleagues examine how tumours engage neural pathways, highlighting implications for cancer progression and therapeutic intervention.

items.title: An insular chain of command
items.author: Jake Rogers
items.content: The functional architecture of the human insula is shown to contain four regions, with an anterior polar region exerting direct influence over posterior pain-related regions.

items.title: Glioma modulation of inhibitory neuron signalling
items.author: Darran Yates
items.content: A new study reports that gliomas can regulate the signalling of inhibitory neurons, promoting tumour progression.

items.title: Reappraising emotion regulation
items.author: Jake Rogers
items.content: The assumed link between cognitive reappraisal and activity in regulatory prefrontal circuits in humans is shown to be absent in task-based functional MRI datasets.
